title: A finite field extension preserves degree after adjoining one indeterminate
statement: Let $E/k$ be a finite extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension], meaning that $E$ has finite dimension as a $k$-vector space. Let $T$ be one indeterminate, and form the rational function fields $k(T)=\operatorname{Frac}(k[T])$ and $E(T)=\operatorname{Frac}(E[T])$ [def-weil-rational-function-field]. Embed $k(T)$ in $E(T)$ by applying $k\hookrightarrow E$ to polynomial coefficients. Then $E(T)/k(T)$ is finite and $[E(T):k(T)]=[E:k]$.
